# Arrays and lists

[Arrays, lists, loops, conditionals and sine]({{ site.baseurl }}/sessions/#b04) · Target weeks 6–7

Generate positions in an ordered collection, then control selected positions with a rule.

**Session and tutorial video:** One teaching session and one tutorial video cover both example files. The second week is for practice. The video has not yet been posted.

Use these example files only as a reference if you are struggling with a step. Build your own file and follow the process one step at a time. Compare the example to understand where you are stuck, then return to your own work. The supplied examples are not files to submit as your assignment.

Select the lesson object and change parameters on the nodes or, where provided, in the GeometryNodes modifier. Press Home over the node editor. Explanations are in Frames and native node names are retained. Build the exercise in a new file of your own, following each step in order.

## Example files and steps

**[Arrays and Lists — Part 1: linear and nested grid]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/03-arrays-lists/Arrays-Lists-Session-1.blend)**

1. Linear loop
2. Nested grid

**[Arrays and Lists — Part 2: arrangements and rules]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/03-arrays-lists/Arrays-Lists-Session-2.blend)**

1. 3D array
2. Hexagonal array
3. Radial array
4. If and range
5. Sine curve

Before hexagonal arrays, the simple 3D array repeats a row into a grid and a grid into layers; Count, Spacing and Cube Size remain exposed. The last scene, Sine curve, uses math along X and Y and repetition in three dimensions to shape a volume of cubes. It introduces the later density and signed-distance lessons while retaining cube instances.

## Short assignment

Reuse your P1b panel as the component in linear, grid, hexagonal and radial studies. Develop three for the sheet, including the nested grid, a conditional change and a sine-driven variation. Include the 3D cube array before hexagonal arrays and compare counts of 3, 4 and 5 per axis.

## Lesson notes and project connection

[Arrays and lists]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/tutorials/u04-arrays-and-lists/) — The panel arrives from P1b and does not change here — only where its copies go. The next unit keeps both the panel and one of these arrangements and replaces the index-based rule with a measurement from an external object. The XYZ array introduces the 3D sampling locations used later for volumes.

Develop this exercise in [P2 — Repetition and response — arrays to attractors]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p2-repetition-and-response-arrays-to-attractors/), P3 — Spatial arrays and assembly — *not yet released*.
